outcomes: An application lists its locales once and every localized route exists at a stable URL per published locale, with the default locale unprefixed
Default text lives next to the code as typed messages, and each locale's catalog records which default text each translation was made from
A published locale is complete: the build refuses a missing, malformed or placeholder-mismatched translation, and reports translations made from a changed default text
Search engines and assistive technology read the language of every page and the address of each of its translations
A locale can have its own paths and its own domain, and a reader who lands on another language than theirs is offered their own
nonGoals: Translating text at request time or calling a translation service from the build
Redirecting a content page because of the reader's browser language or stored preference
Storing the reader's locale preference in browser storage the server cannot read
Calling a model from a Putnami command: the agent of the session translates

requirements.text: The generation configuration's i18n block names well-formed, unique BCP 47 locales that include the default locale; an invalid block fails generation before any route or artifact is written.

Generation registers every layout, page, error and not-found route once per published locale, unprefixed for the default locale and under /<locale> otherwise, except routes matching an excluded pattern, which stay in the default locale only; the render manifest and the HTTP route inventory list each registered route.
A GET request for a route outside the localized set under a locale prefix redirects with 308 to the same path and query without the prefix.
A rendered page carries its route's locale in the html lang attribute, the matching text direction in the dir attribute, and the Content-Language response header when it is rendered per request.

A messages declaration names a namespace and default ICU MessageFormat strings; formatting in a locale uses that locale's catalog text, supports arguments, plural, selectordinal, select, number and date arguments through Intl, and falls back to the default text when the catalog holds no translation, which a production build refuses for a published locale.

A message can wrap part of its text in a named tag such as <link>…</link>; formatting renders each tag through the function passed under its name, the tag functions are typed from the message, and a translation must use the same tags as its default text.

A static page's islands receive the catalog entries of the namespaces the page rendered, and a hydrated page receives its locale's whole catalog because client navigation can render any namespace; both receive their locale only, through script-safe serialization, and the default locale ships no catalog.

Generation keeps each non-default locale catalog aligned with the declared messages, one file per namespace at locales/<locale>/<namespace>.json that names the catalog schema: it adds a missing key, removes a key no declaration holds and the file of a namespace no declaration holds, records the default text a translation was made from, and marks a translation stale when that default text changes, without altering its text.

Generation fails when a published locale lacks a translation, when a message is not valid ICU MessageFormat, or when a translation's arguments differ from its default text's arguments, and warns for each stale translation.

putnami i18n translate writes a work file with every missing and stale entry of each published locale, its default text, a stale entry's old text and translation, its glossary terms and its namespace's other messages. Applying the file writes each answer as a draft, and writes nothing when one answer names an unknown locale, namespace or key, or a validated entry, answers an outdated default text, is not valid ICU MessageFormat, or uses other arguments or tags than its default text.

putnami i18n validate shows a person each draft and stale translation of a locale with its default text and locks each one they accept as validated, recording their git user.name and user.email and the date; it refuses to run without an interactive terminal, inside an agent session, or without a git identity, and validating a stale translation records the current default text as its source.

A localized page's head lists an absolute alternate link per published locale with its hreflang, an x-default alternate to the default locale, a canonical link to itself and its og:locale; a route outside the localized set emits its canonical link only, and a page marked noindex emits none of them.

The locale switcher renders one link per published locale to the same route in that locale, with hreflang and lang attributes and the locale's own name as its text, marks the current locale with aria-current, and carries the choice in a locale query parameter so that following it records the choice without JavaScript.
A Link to an absolute path inside the application resolves under the current page's locale prefix unless it names another locale.

A request for the application root without a locale prefix redirects with 302 and Vary: Accept-Language, Cookie to the locale named by the preference cookie, else the best Accept-Language match, when that locale is not the default; every other path is served in the locale its URL names.

A GET request for a page route whose query names a published locale in its locale parameter sets the locale preference cookie for a year and redirects with 302 and Cache-Control: no-store to the same URL without that parameter; a locale parameter that names no published locale is ignored.

The build writes the sitemap the application serves at /sitemap.xml: one absolute URL per page route without parameters and per pre-rendered path, for each locale a localized route is served in, each with an alternate link per published locale and x-default; a not-found page and a route with parameters but no pre-rendered path are left out.

The i18n.paths block maps a route to its path in a non-default locale: the page is served at the translated path under that locale, its untranslated path under that locale redirects with 308 to the translated one with the query, and links, alternates, the switcher and the sitemap use the translated path; a translated route with parameters, and a translated path that names a locale, is another page's path, leaves the localized set or leaves the layout of its page, fails generation.

The i18n.domains block maps a non-default locale to an origin: a request to that host is served as the locale's prefixed route, every URL built for that locale uses that origin without the prefix, a request under the locale's prefix on the site's host or a locale domain redirects with 308 to the same path and query on the locale's origin, and any other host, such as a development server or a preview, serves the locale under its prefix.

LocaleSuggestion renders nothing on the server; in the browser it shows one line, in the reader's preferred locale, linking to the current page in that locale when the page is published in a locale the reader prefers more than the page's own (the preference cookie, then the browser languages); dismissing it records the page's locale as the choice, and the payload carries its namespace, named by i18n.suggestion, in every published locale.
